\section{Signed CE1/CE2 Reductions}
\label{sec:signed-ce12-reductions}

This section gives the signed center model used by both later methods.  The
propagation interface depending on that model is deferred until after the
transfer calculus in Section~\ref{sec:universal-calculus}.

\subsection{One signed center normal form}

\begin{proposition}[Signed CE1/CE2 center normal form]
\label{prop:signed-center-normal-form}
Let $T_C$ be a closed unit equilateral triangle with
$O\in\interior(T_C)$ and a positive-length boundary trace.  Normalize such a
trace to $e_{0,1}$ and use affine coordinates
\[
 X=V_0+b(V_1-V_0)+a(V_5-V_0).
\]
There are parameters
\[
 0<R<1,
 \qquad
 W=1-R,
\]
\[
 E=\sqrt{1-RW},
 \qquad
 \eta=1-E,
 \qquad
 P=E(1-E),
\]
and nonnegative center slacks $\alpha,\delta$ such that, with
\[
 k=\eta+\alpha+\delta,
\]
the C triangle is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 F_0&=R+\alpha-a+Wb,\\
 F_1&=Rb+Wa-k,\\
 F_2&=W+\delta-b+Ra,
 \end{aligned}}
 \qquad
 T_C=\{F_0,F_1,F_2\ge0\}.
 \label{eq:signed-side-slacks}
\end{equation}
Define
\begin{equation}
 \Delta_R=P-\alpha-W\delta,
 \qquad
 \Delta_L=P-R\alpha-\delta.
 \label{eq:signed-surpluses}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 T_C\cap e_{0,1}
 =\left[\frac{k}{R},W+\delta\right],
 \qquad
 \Haus(T_C\cap e_{0,1})=\frac{\Delta_R}{R},
 \label{eq:signed-right-trace}
\end{equation}
and the possible companion trace is
\begin{equation}
 T_C\cap e_{5,0}
 =\left[\frac{k}{W},R+\alpha\right]
 \quad\text{when }\Delta_L>0,
 \qquad
 \Haus(T_C\cap e_{5,0})=\frac{[\Delta_L]_+}{W}.
 \label{eq:signed-left-trace}
\end{equation}
The normalization requires $\Delta_R>0$, and
\begin{equation}
 T_C\text{ is CE1}\iff\Delta_L\le0,
 \qquad
 T_C\text{ is CE2}\iff\Delta_L>0.
 \label{eq:signed-classification}
\end{equation}
The six center exits, measured from $O$, are
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 d_0^C&=E-\alpha-\delta,&
 d_1^C&=\frac{\delta}{R},&
 d_2^C&=\delta,\\
 d_3^C&=\min\left\{\frac{\alpha}{R},\frac{\delta}{W}\right\},&
 d_4^C&=\alpha,&
 d_5^C&=\frac{\alpha}{W}.
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:signed-center-exits}
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 T_C\cap\{M_0,\ldots,M_5\}=\{M_0\}.
 \label{eq:signed-unique-center-midpoint}
\end{equation}
For closures of original open C triangles one has $\alpha,\delta>0$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[Affine-chart variables]
\label{rem:signed-legacy-variables}
If $\kappa_j=F_j(O)$ denotes the auxiliary side slack in the CE1 affine
chart, take
\[
 \lambda=R,
 \qquad
 s=\frac{k}{R},
 \qquad
 t=W+\delta,
 \qquad
 \kappa_0=\alpha,
 \qquad
 \kappa_2=\delta.
\]
For CE2, take
\[
 x=\frac{k}{W},
 \qquad
 \nu=R+\alpha,
 \qquad
 y=\frac{k}{R},
 \qquad
 v=W+\delta.
\]
If $S=x+y$ and $D=\sqrt{x^2+xy+y^2}$, then
\[
 S=\frac{k}{RW},
 \qquad
 D=\frac{Ek}{RW},
\]
and the old coupling equation is
\[
 (\nu+v)S-xy=D.
\]
Thus the CE1 and CE2 formula lists are two coordinate readings of
Proposition~\ref{prop:signed-center-normal-form}.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Boundary contribution and diameter transfer}

\begin{corollary}[Common center-boundary formula]
\label{cor:signed-center-boundary}
The full center-boundary contribution is
\begin{equation}
 L_{\partial H}(T_C)
 =\frac{\Delta_R}{R}+\frac{[\Delta_L]_+}{W}.
 \label{eq:signed-boundary-length}
\end{equation}
In CE1,
\[
 L_{\partial H}(T_C)
 \le P\le\frac{\sqrt3}{2}-\frac34.
\]
In CE2,
\[
 L_{\partial H}(T_C)
 =\frac{E}{1+E}-\frac{E^2(\alpha+\delta)}{RW}<\frac12.
\]
\end{corollary}

% Proof environment omitted (source: 04a_signed_center_calculus.tex).

\begin{lemma}[Adjacent-edge diameter transfer]
\label{lem:signed-diameter-transfer}
For $0\le q\le1$, the zero-radial forward envelope is
\[
 M_0(q)=\frac{-q+\sqrt{4-3q^2}}2.
\]
Here the argument-free symbol $M_0$ continues to denote the radial midpoint;
$M_0(q)$ denotes the envelope map.
If a unit equilateral triangle reaches parameters $q,b$ on two adjacent
boundary edges, then
\[
 b\le M_0(q).
\]
The map $M_0$ is strictly decreasing.  For $q>0$,
\[
 M_0(q)<1-\frac q2,
 \qquad
 1-M_0(q)>\frac q2.
\]
\end{lemma}

\subsection{The local propagation interface}

For the high-radial parameters used below, $M_c$ is the raw outgoing envelope
and $\Phi_c=1-\overline M_c$ is the following-edge propagation map.  The
latter is nondecreasing and extensive:
\begin{equation}
 \Phi_c(z)\ge z.
 \label{eq:reader-extensive}
\end{equation}
The exact reflection duality is
\begin{equation}
 \Phi_c(a)\le z
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \Phi_c(1-z)\le1-a.
 \label{eq:reader-capped-duality}
\end{equation}

Let a nonsupercritical V triangle have maximal reaches
$(A_i,B_i,C_i)$ with $A_i\ge z$ and $C_i\ge c_i>1/2$.
If the next boundary handoff gives $A_{i+1}\ge1-B_i$, then
\begin{equation}
 A_{i+1}\ge\Phi_{c_i}(z).
 \label{eq:reader-actual-propagation}
\end{equation}
Every composition below abbreviates repeated use of this statement.

\subsection{The common one-gap interface}

\begin{proposition}[Common five-V triangle one-gap reduction]
\label{prop:signed-one-gap-interface}
Assume every V triangle is Vd0, $N_+=1$, and the normalized right center
trace contains a boundary gap, possibly a singleton.  In the CE2 case assume
the companion trace contains no boundary gap.  Put
\[
 X=R-\delta,
 \qquad
 h_0=\frac{k}{2R},
 \qquad
 m_3=\min\left\{\frac\alpha R,\frac\delta W\right\},
\]
and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 c_1&=1-\frac\delta R,&
 c_2&=1-\delta,&
 c_3&=1-m_3,\\
 c_4&=1-\alpha,&
 c_5&=1-\frac\alpha W,&
 c_0&=k.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Let
\[
 z_0=X,
 \qquad
 z_i=\Phi_{c_i}(z_{i-1})
 \quad(1\le i\le5),
\]
and $Z=z_5$.  Then the maximal reaches satisfy
\begin{equation}
 A_0\ge Z,
 \qquad
 A_0\le M_k\left(\frac{k}{R}\right)<1-h_0.
 \label{eq:signed-one-gap-actual}
\end{equation}
The corresponding scalar target is
\begin{equation}
 [\Phi_{1-\alpha}
  \mid \Phi_{1-m_3}
  \mid \Phi_{1-\delta}](h_0)
 >W+\delta.
 \label{eq:signed-three-map-target}
\end{equation}
\end{proposition}

% Proof environment omitted (source: 04a_signed_center_calculus.tex).

The CE1 sign $\Delta_L\le0$ is completed by the selected-$Q_+$ relaxation in
Proposition~\ref{prop:ce1-one-gap}.  We now give the shorter CE2 scalar
clause.

\begin{lemma}[CE2 total slack and two thresholds]
\label{lem:signed-ce2-two-threshold}
Assume $\Delta_R>0$ and $\Delta_L>0$, and put
\[
 T=\alpha+\delta,
 \qquad
 Q=\frac{\eta+T}{2R}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 T<\frac\eta E,
 \label{eq:signed-total-slack}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 \min\{e(\alpha),e(\delta)\}<Q.
 \label{eq:signed-two-threshold}
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

% Proof environment omitted (source: 04a_signed_center_calculus.tex).

\begin{proposition}[Short CE2 one-gap completion]
\label{prop:signed-ce2-one-gap}
\label{thm:s2-geom-r2}
Under the CE2 hypotheses of
Proposition~\ref{prop:signed-one-gap-interface}, the one-gap state is
impossible in either orientation.
\end{proposition}

% Proof environment omitted (source: 04a_signed_center_calculus.tex).

\begin{remark}[Why the CE1 scalar clause remains separate]
The geometric one-gap interface is common, but
\eqref{eq:signed-two-threshold} is not valid on the full CE1 sign domain.
Thus the merger stops at
Proposition~\ref{prop:signed-one-gap-interface}; the CE1 selected-$Q_+$
clause and the CE2 threshold clause require different scalar arguments for
the same target \eqref{eq:signed-three-map-target}.
\end{remark}
}
